claims.text: Europe's sovereignty conversation is mostly about frontier models, giant data centres and GPUs, which it does not control and will not control soon.
claims.quote: The ball today is the frontier model, the giant data centre and the GPU.

claims.text: Building frontier capacity takes years and capital that only benefits those who already have the infrastructure, and most real work does not need a frontier model.
claims.quote: Very few use cases need the frontier

claims.text: Sovereignty is the ability to move: agility, almost liquidity, moving a workload, data and an agent's actions from one provider to another when you decide.
claims.quote: sovereignty is mostly agility, almost liquidity: the ability to move a workload and keep operating

claims.text: Most organisations cannot move, not between clouds and often not within the same hyperscaler, because the infrastructure was hard-coded, created by clicks and never deployed in a second place.
claims.quote: The infrastructure was hard-coded, created by clicks, built up over generations of changes, and never deployed in a second place.

claims.text: The gap is an engineering gap, not a policy gap, and a supplier disruption that stops a business is critical whether or not it is national critical infrastructure.
claims.quote: That is an engineering gap, not a policy gap

claims.text: Draw the Wardley map and ask of each dot you do not control: take it away, what happens; follow the edges up to see the blast radius.
claims.quote: take it away, what happens?

claims.text: If removing a dot stops the service, it is a board-level risk that belongs on the risk register with a name next to it.
claims.quote: by the way, you have a dependency here, and in this scenario you do not have a business

claims.text: The rule applies across the whole stack: a custom-built system only one person can deploy is as much a single point of failure as a supplier, so every dot must be treatable as replaceable.
claims.quote: you must be able to treat every dot as replaceable, at least to the level of a product, whether you built it or bought it

claims.text: Most sovereignty efforts never start because they set the bar at an alternative as good as today; the bar should be that it works, unoptimised, for the minimum viable company.
claims.quote: That is a hundred, and nobody gets from zero to a hundred.

claims.text: The minimum viable company, from the resilience world, is the smallest version of the business that can keep serving customers while the rest recovers.
claims.quote: the smallest version of the business that can keep serving customers while the rest recovers

claims.text: A maturity model for every dot: from 0, it stops, through the data can leave, it runs somewhere once, it runs for the minimum viable company, to 4, it moves when you decide.
claims.quote: A maturity model for every dot you do not control.

claims.text: Having the data is necessary and not sufficient: without the software, the schema and the ability to load and move it, you have an archive, not data mobility.
claims.quote: you do not have data mobility; you have an archive

claims.text: For every dot you do not control you need a twin, compatible enough that the application cannot tell, running on infrastructure you can run; the S3 twin exists today.
claims.quote: something compatible enough that your application cannot tell, running on infrastructure you can run

claims.text: Run the twins in disposable QA environments all the time, so the business proves every week it can run without the dots it does not control and finds problems on a Tuesday, not in an outage.
claims.quote: Every time something breaks, you have found it on a Tuesday, not during an outage.

claims.text: Can it move is the first question; is it cost effective and does it scale is the second, and asking the second first ends sovereignty conversations before they start.
claims.quote: We keep asking the second before the first

claims.text: The engineering benefits of being able to move, reproducible deployments and understood dependencies, will pay for much of the cost even if the alternative runs a little more expensively.
claims.quote: end up paying for much of it, even if the main path stays optimised on the incumbent

claims.text: Only open source, or Creative Commons for content, gives control that survives an acquisition, because a European supplier today is one acquisition from not being one.
claims.quote: Even if a supplier is European today, you are one acquisition away from losing that.

claims.text: Prosus and Dealroom's State of AI in Europe says Europe creates as many new AI startups a year as the US but converts them into breakout companies at a third of the rate.
claims.quote: but it converts them into breakout companies at a third of the rate

value.unit: times lower conversion rate to breakout companies

claims.text: Stanford's study of the founders of 500 American unicorns found 44% were born outside the US, with the UK, Germany and France leading the European countries of birth.
claims.quote: found that 44% were born outside the US

value.unit: percent of unicorn founders born outside the US

claims.text: Europe's gap is not startups or talent but a commercial open source model that connects many small players into a bigger play.
claims.quote: The gap is positioning, and it is a commercial open source model that Europe never quite developed

claims.text: Some twins should be provided centrally, by governments, industry bodies or the larger organisations in a supply chain, as a road: built once, open, used by everyone.
claims.quote: built once, open, used by everyone, and not a central project that becomes another dependency

claims.text: The analysis was always right and always too expensive; with today's models the mapping and simulations can be done at scale, better on twins than in a spreadsheet.
claims.quote: With today's models the mapping and the simulations can finally be done at scale

claims.text: The map in the figure is illustrative, a typical service rather than a measured one.
claims.quote: The map in the figure is illustrative.

claims.text: The maturity levels are a proposal and have not been calibrated across organisations.
claims.quote: The maturity levels are a proposal.

claims.text: The startup and founder figures are other people's: parity in startup numbers, not more, and a unicorn study to 2021 not specific to AI.
claims.quote: The startup and founder figures are other people's.

claims.text: The minimum viable company is not the owner's term; what is his is running it on twins in QA.
claims.quote: The minimum viable company is not my term.

claims.text: Twins beyond storage are not built; the S3 twin exists and most of the others are the work to do.
claims.quote: Twins beyond storage are not built.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 12 October 2026, after a day at a sovereignty event, written by the site's agent.
claims.quote: A voice memo of mine on 12 October 2026, after a day at a sovereignty event
